record.paper_title: Billiard dynamics: A survey with the emphasis on open problems
record.original_question: For an arbitrary Birkhoff billiard table Y, let Φ be the phase space of the billiard map, let P be the set of all periodic points, let P_n be the set of periodic points of exact period n, and let μ be the Liouville measure on Φ. Must μ(P)=0?

evidence.quote: Задача 3. Пусть Y — произвольный биллиардный стол Биркгофа. а) Доказать, что μ(P)=0.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $Y \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a Birkhoff billiard table, i.e., a strictly convex bounded planar domain with sufficiently smooth boundary $\partial Y$. The associated billiard map $T \colon \Phi \to \Phi$ is defined on the phase space
$$\Phi = \{(q,v) : q \in \partial Y,\ v \text{ a unit vector pointing into } Y\},$$
which can be parametrized by $(s,\theta)$ with $s$ an arclength coordinate on $\partial Y$ and $\theta \in (0,\pi)$ the angle between $v$ and the positive tangent to $\partial Y$. The map $T$ preserves the Liouville measure $d\mu = \sin\theta\, ds\, d\theta$ on $\Phi$. For each integer $n \ge 2$, let
$$P_n = \{x \in \Phi : T^n(x) = x \text{ and } T^k(x) \neq x \text{ for } 1 \le k < n\}$$
be the set of periodic points of exact period $n$, and let $P = \bigcup_{n \ge 2} P_n$ denote the set of all periodic points of $T$.

Prove or disprove: for every Birkhoff billiard table $Y$, one has $\mu(P) = 0$.
artifact.status_search_result: This is the classical Ivrii conjecture (1980). It is known to hold in several special cases—e.g., for analytic convex boundaries, for generic algebraic domains, and for low-period cases (period 3 settled by Rychlik and others; period 4 by Glutsyuk–Kudryashov)—but the general conjecture for arbitrary smooth Birkhoff billiard tables remains open. Counterexamples exist only in the broader class of projective billiards, not for ordinary Birkhoff billiards.

status_evidence.title: Ivrii's conjecture for some cases in outer and symplectic billiards
status_evidence.snippet: The Ivrii conjecture (1980) predicts that no billiard has a positive-measure set of periodic points... proofs for (2n+1,n) and (2n,n-1)-periodic cases for outer billiards.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture remains a conjecture in general; only special cases proven.

status_evidence.title: Examples of projective billiards with open sets of periodic orbits
status_evidence.snippet: In the class of projective billiards, counter-examples to Ivrii's conjecture have been exhibited.
status_evidence.claim: Counterexamples exist only in the broader projective billiards setting, not in classical Birkhoff billiards.

status_evidence.title: Algebraic billiards in the Fermat hyperbola
status_evidence.snippet: For generic complex billiards of degree d ≥ 2, the set of complex periodic points has measure 0, proving the Ivrii Conjecture for the classical billiard map in generic algebraic domains.
status_evidence.claim: Ivrii's conjecture proven for generic algebraic domains, still open in full generality.
